alignments.note: Case preposition rides with the article, headed on *the* (rules 17, 21).
Second attributive article governing an expressed head noun; the participle carries the supplied relativizer, so the article realizes nothing (rules 23, 31).
No genitive pronoun competes, so the article is what *his* realizes (rule 20, second arm).
Participle rendered as a finite relative clause; *that* is its helper (rule 31).

εἰς … μέσον → the single word *forth*, which answers to neither token separately, so rules 45 and 94 make the pair one unit headed on the governed word. The competing reading gives *Stand forth* whole to Ἔγειρε and leaves all three tokens of εἰς τὸ μέσον unrepresented; I took this one because *forth* renders the directional phrase and not the verb's own sense (the projection's gloss is *Arise into the midst*).
A noncompositional unit never absorbs an intervening article, which contributes no part of the fused English word (rule 93).

review_notes: The ASV compresses Ἔγειρε εἰς τὸ μέσον into *Stand forth*; I split it as *Stand* plus a noncompositional εἰς/μέσον, with τό unrepresented under rule 93.
τὴν χεῖρα → *his hand* takes the possessive on the article under rule 20's second arm.
